name: Djemaa El-Fna
blurb: Medina's main square, the highlight of any Marrakech night: storytellers, musicians and food stalls.
when: Open all day; best in the evening

name: The Souks
blurb: Market lanes beside Djemaa El-Fna selling spices, leather, lamps and clothes; haggle hard, as tourists are often quoted higher prices.
when: Daytime and evening; hours not listed

name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
blurb: One of North Africa's largest madrasas, completed in 1564-65 and full of decorative art; cheap to visit.
priceText: 50 dirham adult; children under 12 10 dirham; groups over 20 pay 30 dirham each

name: Majorelle Gardens
blurb: Cobalt-blue garden and studio created by painter Jacques Majorelle; tickets are sold online only.
priceText: 170 dirham; 30 dirham extra for the Berber Museum

name: Bahia Palace
blurb: Late-19th-century palace of courtyards, gardens and richly decorated rooms; a good look at Moroccan architecture.

name: Saadian Tombs
blurb: Royal necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty, with decorated chambers such as the Chamber of the Twelve Columns.

name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum
blurb: Museum dedicated to designer Yves Saint Laurent; ticket queues are shorter than at Majorelle, but tickets must be booked online.
priceText: 120 dirham; combination ticket with Majorelle Gardens and Berber Museum 180 dirham

name: Hamam Essalama
blurb: Basic local hammam where entry is cheap and a scrub costs extra; staff speak neither English nor French.

name: Chez Chegrouni
blurb: Budget couscous house known for its vegetarian version and very generous portions; usually full of tourists.

name: Chesterfield Pub
blurb: Odd 'English pub' in a palm-tree courtyard with an outdoor pool; serves Moroccan lager to a mostly local crowd.

name: Souk El Had
blurb: Huge market with 3,000+ stalls for fruit, spices, leather and souvenirs; touts approach tourists at the main gates.

name: Agadir Kasbah (Fortress)
blurb: Surviving part of the old fortress on the hill beside town; walk up or take a taxi (30–50 dirham).

name: Agadir beach
blurb: Large town beach that is usually not crowded; it can be very windy, as in February, so bring a layer.

name: Surfing around Agadir
blurb: Surf breaks such as Imsouane, Devil's Rock and Anchor Point, with many surf schools and camps nearby.

name: Memory of Agadir Museum
blurb: Small photo museum on the 29 February 1960 earthquake; the sign is missing, so look for the iron gates.

name: Museum Municipal du Patrimoine Amazigh
blurb: Small municipal museum of Berber objects: old instruments, jewellery, traditional clothing and manuscripts.

name: K-moon
blurb: Small restaurant serving excellent wood-fire grilled meat with many small side bowls; quick, efficient service.

name: Herguita
blurb: Restaurant with an ocean view and typical local food; the brochettes (skewers) are the ones to order.

name: Rotisserie Al Marché
blurb: Authentic Moroccan street-food counter known for its sandwiches; a cheap, quick bite.

name: Tunis Medina
blurb: UNESCO-listed old town of narrow lanes, decorated houses, vaults and vendors; walk only, and get lost on purpose.

name: Bab El Bahr
blurb: Sea gate of 1848 on Avenue de France; its site once had the Mediterranean on one side and Lake Tunis on the other.

name: Dar Ben Abdallah Museum
blurb: Folk museum in an 18th-century medina palace, showing a rich merchant's Ottoman-era life through faience, costumes and furniture.

name: Bardo Museum
blurb: Former bey's palace renowned for its Roman mosaics; the collection covers prehistory through the Ottoman period.

name: Uthina Roman ruins
blurb: Roman-Berber city ruins outside Tunis: theatre, amphitheatre, triumphal arch and many mosaics; a day trip.

name: Halfaouine food market
blurb: Cheap, traditional food market at Place Halfaouine near the railway station; good for a simple local meal.

name: La Sirène
blurb: Pick your fish at the market counter and it is fried on the spot; water views, but it fills up, so expect a wait.

name: Panorama Medina
blurb: Decorated tea house with a big rooftop over the medina and its mosques; cheap tea and shisha.
priceText: DT2 for tea, DT5 for shisha

name: Le Boeuf sur le Toit
blurb: Trendy spot for food, drinks, live music and DJs, with a dance floor; its name means 'the Ox on the Roof'.

name: Bar Jamaica
blurb: Funky bar on the 10th floor of Hotel el-Hana International, with music and outdoor seating; locals and foreigners mix.

name: Dubai Fountain
blurb: 270 m dancing fountain by the Dubai Mall, with a jet reaching about 150 m; the night shows are the ones to see.
when: Night shows every 30 min from 18:00 (to 22:00 weekdays, 23:00 weekends)

name: Gold Souk and Spice Souk
blurb: Historic markets at the mouth of Dubai Creek: the gold souk sells gold in large quantities, the spice souk has faded.

name: Abra crossing on Dubai Creek
blurb: Traditional wooden water taxi across Dubai Creek between Bur Dubai and Deira, the classic cheap ride between the old souks.
priceText: Dh1 per ride; Dh2 on air-conditioned boats (press report, late 2025)

name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
blurb: One of the last pockets of old Dubai, with reconstructed houses in the traditional style; the atmosphere is the draw.

name: Dubai Museum
blurb: Dubai's social history, displayed in and under Al Fahidi Fort; a must if you want the emirate's back story.

name: Burj Khalifa (At The Top)
blurb: World's tallest building at 828 m; the observation decks on levels 124–125 need a timed slot, which often sells out.
priceText: Silver tier from about AED 188 (reseller listings, 2026)
when: Timed slots; book ahead (hours not checked)

name: Dubai Frame
blurb: Two 150 m towers joined by a bridge, with a museum and gallery on Dubai's growth from fishing village to city.
priceText: From AED 49 when booked online (adult); children 3–12 AED 25

name: Jumeirah Beach walking and cycling track
blurb: About 7 km of coastal track from Dubai Canal to Burj Al Arab, shared by Emirati families and expats.

name: Zero Gravity
blurb: Beach club for a party; no entry fee, but a beer costs 50 dirham.

name: Ravi Restaurant
blurb: Cheap, no-frills Pakistani and Indian food in Bur Dubai; a good stop if you like it spicy.

name: Bath No. 5 (public bath)
blurb: Cheap public bath in the sulphur district with a hot pool and sauna; separate men's and women's sections.

name: Old Tbilisi
blurb: Old town of balconied houses, ancient churches and winding lanes; the walk is the point, with odd sights along the way.

name: Sameba Cathedral
blurb: Holy Trinity Cathedral built 1995-2004; the third-tallest Orthodox cathedral, blending traditional Georgian styles.

name: Narikala Fortress
blurb: Crumbling hilltop fortress with panoramic views over Tbilisi; a steep climb, or take the cable car.

name: Mtatsminda Park
blurb: Hilltop park with views over Tbilisi and a Ferris wheel; the funicular is paid with the park's access card.
priceText: Access card 2 lari; funicular 10 lari one way

name: Museum of Georgia
blurb: Part of the National Museum: Caucasian archaeology and ethnography from the Bronze Age to the early 20th century.
priceText: Adults 7 lari, students 1 lari, guided tour in English 45 lari

name: Dry Bridge flea market
blurb: Antiques, jewellery, instruments and electronics; haggling is expected and the market runs until sunset.

name: Shawarma joint (city centre)
blurb: No-name shawarma place among pricier tourist restaurants; the 'small' one is big enough for a full meal.

name: Alibi Room
blurb: Cheap bar popular with young locals; it fills up on Fridays and can get rough, so not for the faint-hearted.

name: Bassiani
blurb: Famous underground techno club, often compared to Berlin's Berghain; entry is up to the door staff.
priceText: 30 lari entry (if the bouncer lets you in)

name: Cafesjian Museum of Modern Art
blurb: Modern art with Gorky, Warhol and Chagall, plus a strong glass-art collection; the escalator gallery is open every day.
when: Escalator gallery daily 08:00–20:00; special galleries Fri–Sun 10:00–20:00

name: Armenian Genocide Memorial (Tsitsernakaberd)
blurb: Memorial and museum for victims of the 1915 Armenian Genocide; the hilltop monument is open at all times.

name: Matenadaran
blurb: World's largest collection of Armenian illuminated manuscripts, with a display room of the finest pieces.

name: History Museum of Armenia
blurb: National history from early settlements to the 20th century, with plenty of archaeology and art along the timeline.

name: Cascades and Sculpture Park
blurb: Sculpture park by the Opera with Botero and other international works, part of the Cafesjian Centre for the Arts.

name: Republic Square
blurb: Yerevan's main square, a grand Soviet-era ensemble of neo-classical government buildings with Armenian touches.

name: Vernissage weekend market
blurb: Weekend open-air market in the park between Aram and Buzand streets: rugs, paintings, souvenirs, instruments and more.

name: Master Class
blurb: Small, focused menu; the Angus beef kebab sandwiches are the thing to order for a cheap, filling meal.

name: Grand Candy Ponchikanots
blurb: Ponchik shop in a former Soviet ponchik spot: fried dough with custard and powdered sugar, a sweet local classic.

name: Calumet
blurb: Bohemian, friendly ethnic lounge bar with English-speaking staff and a solid drinks list; very smoky, no outdoor area.

name: Santa Claus Village
blurb: Built close to the Arctic Circle, open every day of the year to meet Santa; touristy, but a classic stop.

name: Ounasvaara winter walking trail
blurb: Six-kilometre winter walking trail through forest on Ounasvaara hill; keep off the ski tracks.

name: Kotatieva Winter Leisure Park
blurb: Outdoor park built around a 500 m ice-skating track; open from December to March.

name: Taava Reindeer Farm (reindeer safari)
blurb: Three-hour daytime reindeer safari from the farm, about 30 minutes' drive from town; the farm visit is the cheaper option.
priceText: From 160 € daytime reindeer safari (3 h); farm visit from 79 € (1 h 30 min)
when: Safari 3 h; start times not listed

name: Korundi House of Culture
blurb: Art museum mostly of modern Finnish art, with concerts and culture events; home of the Lapland Chamber Orchestra.
priceText: €8 adult, €5 students, €3 children (7–15); Museum Card valid

name: Lapland Brewery
blurb: Finland's northernmost brewery, founded 2016; tours cost €20–25. Listed hours cover Monday to Saturday.

name: Kansan Pubi
blurb: Cheap pub, popular with young locals; gets busy on weekend evenings before people head out to clubs.
priceText: Free admission, €3.5 for a 0.4-L domestic beer

name: Roy Club (Roippari)
blurb: Known locally as Roippari: small nightclub open every day since 1985, karaoke on the ground floor, dancing in the cellar. 18+.

name: Pub Pisto
blurb: Stylish pub open since 1960 and a local institution; it appears in many of Jari Tervo's novels.

name: Pizzeria Trocadero
blurb: Famous for oversized pizzas, reputedly the biggest in Rovaniemi; a filling, simple meal.
